title: Environment Setup and Tooling
description: Learn how to set up the React Native development environment on your system, including installing necessary tools and running your first app.

lessons.title: Prerequisites for React Native
lessons.content: Before starting with React Native, you should have a basic understanding of JavaScript and React. Familiarity with mobile platforms (Android/iOS) is helpful but not necessary.

lessons.title: Installing Node.js and npm
lessons.content:
Download and install Node.js from https://nodejs.org/
To check installation:
```bash
node -v
npm -v
```

lessons.title: Installing Expo CLI
lessons.content:
Expo CLI is the easiest way to start with React Native:
```bash
npm install -g expo-cli
```

lessons.title: Setting Up Android Studio (for Android Development)
lessons.content: Install Android Studio, then install Android SDK and configure environment variables (e.g., ANDROID_HOME). This setup is essential for running apps on Android emulators or physical devices.

lessons.title: Setting Up Xcode (for iOS Development)
lessons.content: Install Xcode from the Mac App Store. Xcode includes all the tools required for iOS development, including the iOS simulator.

lessons.title: Creating a New Project with Expo
lessons.content:
```bash
expo init MyFirstApp
cd MyFirstApp
expo start
```

lessons.title: Running the App on Emulator or Device
lessons.content:
- Use Android Emulator or iOS Simulator.
- Or scan the QR code with the Expo Go app on your phone to run the app instantly.

lessons.title: Using Visual Studio Code
lessons.content: Visual Studio Code is a powerful editor with React Native support. Install extensions like 'React Native Tools' for enhanced development experience.

lessons.title: Debugging React Native Apps
lessons.content:
- Use console.log for quick debugging.
- Use Expo Developer Tools for inspecting logs and performance.
- React Native Debugger can be connected for advanced debugging.

lessons.title: Common Setup Errors and Fixes
lessons.content:
- Metro bundler not found: Restart your terminal.
- Android emulator not detected: Ensure it's running before `expo start`.
- Permission issues: Run commands with admin rights if needed.
